paper.title_en: Three-gluon vertex planar degeneracy: a perturbative explanation
paper.abstract_en: We provide a perturbative explanation for the planar degeneracy of the three-gluon vertex in Yang-Mills theory, using the Curci-Ferrari (CF) model in the Landau gauge. By employing an infrared safe renormalization scheme whose coupling remains regular at all scales, we perform a one-loop calculation for arbitrary kinematics in both three and four dimensions. Our results demonstrate that the observed planar degeneracy can be understood naturally due to perturbative reasons: i) the tree-level form factor dominates the vertex structure simply because perturbative corrections are suppressed; ii) the one loop corrections to this form factor remain remarkably flat across the allowed phase space. We quantify the deviations from the symmetric configuration, finding that the mean error of the symmetric approximation, in the case of the tree-level form factor, peaks at approximately 3% both in three and four dimensions, with the most significant departures occurring near soft-gluon configurations due to tamed ultraviolet collinear divergences. This work explains previous lattice and Dyson-Schwinger studies while reinforcing the capacity of the mass-extended Faddeev-Popov Lagrangian to capture complex infrared QCD dynamics through perturbative analytical techniques.
